message: Hi, I'm a student with a distro making certification background. My overall academic average is 79% in an IT/computer-science degree. I'm interested in cloud computing and cloud computing. I want to become a Web Developer. My family can afford at most about USD 3500 per year. I live in Bengaluru. I'm open to anywhere in India. Getting a good job after graduation matters more to me than anything else.
explanation:
This MTech in Computer Networks is highly relevant to your interest in cloud computing and web development, as it covers 'networking_cloud' and 'software_engineering.' The tuition of $2050 fits well within your family's budget, and the program requires a CS background, matching your qualifications. This option offers excellent technical depth while maintaining a low cost, making job placement a strong possibility.

The MCA program is an ideal choice for aspiring Web Developers due to its focus on 'software_engineering.' With a very low annual tuition of $1350 and a minimum grade requirement of 74%, it respects your financial constraints while building core development skills. This option provides strong technical training, making job placement highly probable.

This MSc in Human-Computer Interaction offers a blend of design and development through its focus on 'software_engineering' and 'design_hci.' The tuition ($2250) is affordable, and the program’s curriculum aligns with modern web development roles. The main trade-off here is that it emphasizes user experience (HCI) more than pure backend cloud infrastructure.

If you are open to data roles, this MTech in Data Engineering is a strong contender. It has an affordable tuition of $3250 and accepts students with your background (no CS requirement). While the focus is on 'data_science_analytics,' it provides excellent job prospects in high-demand tech sectors like Bengaluru.

This MSc in Information Systems offers a broad foundation in 'business_information_systems,' making it a safe and affordable option ($2400). It is suitable if you want to combine your technical skills with business understanding. The trade-off is that the focus is more on general IT management rather than deep specialization in cloud or web development.
